title: Internet Protocol, Version 6 (IPv6) Specification

hero.subtitle: The next generation Internet Protocol with 128-bit addressing

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
IPv6 is the successor to IPv4, designed to address the exhaustion of IPv4 addresses and to incorporate improvements based on decades of operational experience with IPv4. The most visible change is the increase from 32-bit to 128-bit addresses, providing a virtually unlimited address space.

With 2^128 possible addresses (approximately 3.4 x 10^38), IPv6 provides enough addresses for every grain of sand on Earth to have a trillion addresses each. This effectively eliminates address scarcity as a design constraint.
sections.eli5: IPv6 is the new, bigger addressing system for the internet, made so we do not run out of addresses.

sections.title: Terminology
sections.content:
NodeA device that implements IPv6
RouterA node that forwards IPv6 packets not explicitly addressed to itself
HostAny node that is not a router
LinkA communication facility over which nodes can communicate at the link layer
MTUMaximum Transmission Unit - largest packet size (in octets) on a link
sections.eli5: A few names used throughout: a node is any device that speaks IPv6, a router passes packets along, and a host is a node that is not a router.

sections.title: Header Format
sections.content:
The IPv6 header is a streamlined, fixed 40-byte structure. Unlike IPv4, there are no header checksums (delegated to upper layers) and no fragmentation fields in the base header.

Feature
IPv4
IPv6
Header Size
20-60 bytes (variable)
40 bytes (fixed)
Address Size
32 bits
128 bits
Checksum
Yes
No (removed)
Fragmentation
Routers may fragment
Source only
sections.eli5: Every IPv6 packet starts with the same size envelope, 40 bytes, with the same boxes in the same places. Extras that IPv4 squeezed into the envelope go elsewhere.

sections.title: Extension Headers
sections.content:
IPv6 replaces IPv4's variable-length options with a daisy-chain of extension headers. Each header contains a Next Header field identifying the type of the following header.

Hop-by-Hop OptionsProcessed by every node along the pathNH: 0
RoutingLists intermediate nodes to visit (source routing)NH: 43
FragmentFragmentation and reassembly (source only)NH: 44
Destination OptionsOptions processed only by destinationNH: 60
AuthenticationIPsec authentication headerNH: 51
ESPIPsec encapsulating security payloadNH: 50

Extension headers MUST be processed in the order they appear. Only the Hop-by-Hop Options header is examined by every node along the path; the other extension headers are not examined or processed until the packet reaches the node named in the Destination Address field.
sections.eli5: Extra instructions are stapled behind the main envelope like a chain of notes, each one saying what kind of note comes next.

sections.title: Flow Labels
sections.content:
The 20-bit Flow Label field in the IPv6 header enables efficient handling of real-time traffic flows. Routers can use the combination of source address and flow label to identify packets belonging to the same flow without inspecting transport-layer headers.

Flow Identification
A flow is a sequence of packets sent from a source to a destination for which the source desires special handling by intervening routers.
Non-zero Values
A source labeling a new flow chooses its flow label pseudo-randomly and uniformly from 1 to FFFFF hex; packets that do not belong to a flow carry zero.
Router Processing
Hosts and routers that do not support flow labels must set the field to zero when originating a packet, pass it on unchanged when forwarding, and ignore it when receiving.
sections.eli5: A sender can put the same sticker on all the packets in one stream, like a video call, so routers can treat them together without opening them.

sections.title: Address Architecture
sections.content:
IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long, written as eight groups of four hexadecimal digits separated by colons. The address architecture defines three types of addresses:

UnicastIdentifies a single interface; packets delivered to that interface
MulticastIdentifies a group of interfaces; packets delivered to all members
AnycastIdentifies a group; packets delivered to the nearest member
IPv6 Address Examples
Full form:    2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334
Compressed:   2001:db8:85a3::8a2e:370:7334
Loopback:     ::1
Link-local:   fe80::1
sections.eli5: IPv6 addresses are very long, written as eight groups of letters and numbers. There are addresses for one place, for a whole group, and for the nearest of a group.

subtitle: The next generation Internet Protocol with 128-bit addressing

tldr.problem: IPv4's 32-bit addresses were running out, and its variable-length header made routers' work harder.
tldr.mechanism: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses and a fixed 40-byte header with no checksum, moves optional features into chained extension headers, and adds a flow label for traffic that needs special handling.
tldr.outcome: A vastly larger address space and a simpler header to process, though it is not directly compatible with IPv4. RFC 8200 has since replaced this document.

eli5.summary: The internet was running out of house numbers, so IPv6 invents much longer ones, with so many that nobody should run out again. It also makes the address label on every parcel the same size, so the post office can read it faster.

today: IPv6 is deployed alongside IPv4 on most major networks and is built into every mainstream operating system. RFC 2460 was obsoleted by RFC 8200 in 2017, which kept the protocol the same and is now the Internet Standard (STD 86). The address architecture described here lives in a separate RFC (now RFC 4291).

implementations.name: Wireshark and tcpdump
implementations.note: Both decode IPv6 headers and extension headers.

fields.name: Traffic Class
fields.desc: 8-bit traffic class field, available for originating nodes and forwarding routers to identify and distinguish classes or priorities of packets.

fields.name: Flow Label
fields.desc: 20-bit flow label. Zero for packets that do not belong to a flow; see section 6.
fields.value: 0 or a random non-zero flow label

fields.name: Payload Length
fields.desc: Length of the IPv6 payload, the rest of the packet following this 40-byte header, in octets. Extension headers count as part of the payload.

fields.name: Next Header
fields.desc: 8-bit selector identifying the type of header immediately following the IPv6 header. Uses the same values as the IPv4 Protocol field.

fields.name: Hop Limit
fields.desc: 8-bit unsigned integer, decremented by 1 by each node that forwards the packet. The packet is discarded if it reaches zero.

fields.name: Source Address
fields.desc: 128-bit address of the originator of the packet.

fields.name: Destination Address
fields.desc: 128-bit address of the intended recipient of the packet (possibly not the ultimate recipient if a Routing header is present).
